title: USDA forecasts and projections (WASDE, ERS farm income forecasts, USDA Agricultural Baseline)
agency: U.S. Department of Agriculture: World Agricultural Outlook Board (WAOB, Office of the Chief Economist) and Economic Research Service (ERS)
keywords: world agricultural supply and demand estimates
questions: latest USDA projection of U.S. corn ending stocks for the current marketing year
how the WASDE soybean export forecast changed from month to month
world wheat production forecast by country
USDA's 2026 net farm income forecast, nominal and inflation-adjusted
how accurate were past net farm income forecasts
USDA 10-year baseline projection of corn planted acres and prices

manual.how: Download the files in a browser and upload them unchanged. WASDE: the monthly CSV https://www.usda.gov/sites/default/files/documents/oce-wasde-report-data-YYYY-MM.csv (January 2021 on), or for older or missing months the consolidated CSV on the Historical WASDE Report Data page (https://www.usda.gov/oce/commodity-markets/wasde/historical-wasde-report-data). Farm income: the release ZIP ('September 3, 2026 release'), the 'U.S. farm sector financial indicators' .xlsx or the data archive ZIP on https://www.ers.usda.gov/data-products/farm-income-and-wealth-statistics/data-files-us-and-state-level-farm-income-and-wealth-statistics. Baseline: the ZIP under 'File Downloads' on https://www.ers.usda.gov/data-products/agricultural-baseline-database.

cache.why: Each WASDE month and each farm income release is a new vintage that revises the last; data/ is reused per run only.

redistribution.why: WASDE, ERS farm income statistics and the USDA baseline are U.S. government works in the public domain (17 U.S.C. 105); USDA asks for attribution.

citation: U.S. Department of Agriculture, {dataset}, usda.gov / ers.usda.gov, retrieved {retrieved_long}.
clarify: Which vintage? WASDE is reissued monthly and ERS farm income forecasts three times a year (February, early September, early December); the default is the latest, and a comparison over time needs one vintage per release.
Nominal or inflation-adjusted dollars? ERS publishes nominal values plus a chain-type GDP price index (latest year = 100); the default is nominal.
Which marketing year (WASDE) or calendar year (farm income)? Marketing years differ by commodity (corn and soybeans September-August, wheat June-May, cotton and rice August-July).
